events.description: About 2.3 million stone blocks were used. It is the oldest and only surviving wonder of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
events.significance: Icon of ancient engineering.

events.title: Code of Hammurabi
events.summary: One of the earliest and most complete written legal codes.
events.description: King Hammurabi of Babylon inscribed 282 laws on a basalt stele, including the principle of proportional punishment.
events.significance: A milestone in the history of law.

events.title: Shang Dynasty Oracle Bones
events.summary: The earliest Chinese writing appears on oracle bones used in divination.
events.description: Shang kings asked questions of ancestors by heating turtle shells and ox bones; the inscriptions are ancestors of modern Chinese characters.
events.significance: The origin of the Chinese script.

events.title: Athenian Democracy
events.summary: Cleisthenes’ reforms gave Athenian citizens a direct say in government.
events.description: Citizens voted in the Assembly on the Pnyx hill. Athens produced philosophers like Socrates, Plato and Aristotle, and the Parthenon.
events.significance: A foundational idea for later democratic thought.

events.title: The Buddha and the Rise of Buddhism
events.summary: Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and taught the Middle Way.
events.description: Buddhism spread across South Asia and later to Sri Lanka, Central, East and Southeast Asia. Bengal under the Palas became one of its greatest centres.
events.significance: One of the world’s major religions.

events.title: Confucius
events.summary: The philosopher whose teachings on ethics and government shaped East Asia.
events.description: Collected in the Analects, his ideas on family duty, ritual and benevolent rule became the basis of Chinese education and civil service.
events.significance: Shaped East Asian society for over two millennia.

events.title: Conquests of Alexander the Great
events.summary: Alexander conquered the Persian Empire and reached the Indus within 11 years.
events.description: He defeated Darius III at Issus and Gaugamela, founded Alexandria in Egypt and fought King Porus at the Hydaspes before his army refused to go further.
events.significance: Spread Greek culture across the East (the Hellenistic age).

events.title: Maurya Empire and Ashoka
events.summary: After the bloody Kalinga war, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and ruled by dhamma.
events.description: His edicts, carved on rocks and pillars across South Asia, promoted non-violence and welfare. The Mahasthan Brahmi inscription in Bangladesh dates to the Mauryan era.
events.significance: The first empire uniting most of the subcontinent.

events.title: Qin Unifies China
events.summary: Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor of a united China.
events.description: He standardised script, weights, coinage and axle widths, linked early walls that became the Great Wall, and was buried with the Terracotta Army.
events.significance: Created the imperial Chinese state.

events.title: Roman Republic to Empire
events.summary: Rome grew from a city-state into a Mediterranean power; Augustus became the first emperor in 27 BCE.
events.description: The Republic defeated Carthage in the Punic Wars. Julius Caesar’s dictatorship and assassination (44 BCE) led to civil war and Octavian’s rise as Augustus.
events.significance: Founded the Roman Empire and its legal legacy.

events.title: Han Dynasty Opens the Silk Road
events.summary: Zhang Qian’s missions opened trade routes linking China to Central Asia and the Mediterranean.
events.description: Silk, spices, paper, glass, horses and religions (Buddhism, Islam, Christianity) moved along the network for 1,500 years.
events.significance: The first great network of Eurasian globalisation.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.summary: The Germanic leader Odoacer deposed the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
events.description: Economic crisis, migration and division weakened the West. The Eastern (Byzantine) Empire continued until 1453.
events.significance: Traditionally marks the end of antiquity in Europe.

references.title: Wikipedia – Fall of the Western Roman Empire

events.title: Justinian and Hagia Sophia
events.summary: Emperor Justinian built the Hagia Sophia and codified Roman law.
events.description: The Corpus Juris Civilis became the basis of civil law in Europe. Hagia Sophia’s dome was an engineering marvel for nearly a thousand years.
events.significance: The height of the early Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Tang Dynasty Golden Age
events.summary: Tang China was a cosmopolitan empire of poetry, trade and Buddhism.
events.description: Chang’an was among the world’s largest cities. The Tang fought the Abbasids at Talas (751). Poets Li Bai and Du Fu flourished, and woodblock printing developed.
events.significance: A high point of Chinese civilisation.

events.title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
events.summary: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor in Rome.
events.description: Charlemagne united much of Western Europe and sponsored the Carolingian Renaissance of learning. He exchanged embassies with Harun al-Rashid.
events.significance: The foundation of the Holy Roman Empire idea.

events.title: Viking Age Begins
events.summary: Scandinavian raiders attacked the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793.
events.description: Vikings raided, traded and settled from North America (Vinland) to Baghdad, founded Kievan Rus’, and settled in Normandy, Iceland and Greenland.
events.significance: Reshaped northern Europe.

events.title: Song Dynasty Innovations
events.summary: Song China pioneered paper money, movable type, the magnetic compass and gunpowder weapons.
events.description: Bi Sheng invented movable type around 1040; the compass was used for navigation; a huge commercial economy grew.
events.significance: Inventions that changed the world.

events.title: The Crusades
events.summary: European Christians launched military expeditions to the Levant.
events.description: The First Crusade captured Jerusalem in 1099. Salahuddin retook it in 1187, and the fall of Acre in 1291 ended the Crusader states.
events.significance: Two centuries of conflict and exchange between Europe and the Muslim world.

events.title: Genghis Khan and the Mongol Empire
events.summary: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan and built the largest contiguous land empire in history.
events.description: Mongol armies conquered China, Central Asia, Persia and Russia. The Pax Mongolica revived Silk Road trade but conquest caused vast destruction, including Baghdad in 1258.
events.significance: Connected Eurasia like never before.

events.title: Magna Carta
events.summary: English barons forced King John to accept limits on royal power.
events.description: Clauses guaranteeing that no free man would be imprisoned without lawful judgment became a symbol of the rule of law.
events.significance: A foundation of constitutional government.

events.title: The Black Death
events.summary: Bubonic plague killed an estimated 30–50% of Europe’s population.
events.description: Spread along trade routes from Central Asia and the Black Sea, the pandemic also devastated the Middle East and North Africa, transforming labour, religion and society.
events.significance: The deadliest pandemic in recorded history.

events.title: Voyages of Zheng He
events.summary: The Muslim admiral led seven Ming treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean.
events.description: With hundreds of ships, Zheng He visited Southeast Asia, Bengal, India, Arabia and East Africa, exchanging gifts and envoys.
events.significance: The largest naval expeditions before modern times.

events.title: Gutenberg’s Printing Press
events.summary: Johannes Gutenberg developed movable-type printing in Europe.
events.description: The Gutenberg Bible (c. 1455) began a revolution in information. Within 50 years millions of books had been printed.
events.significance: Enabled the Renaissance, Reformation and Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
events.summary: Sailing for Castile, Columbus landed in the Bahamas.
events.description: The voyage began sustained European contact with the Americas, the Columbian Exchange of crops and animals, and the catastrophic decline of indigenous populations through disease and conquest.
events.significance: Connected the two halves of the globe.

events.title: Vasco da Gama Reaches India
events.summary: A Portuguese fleet sailed around Africa to India.
events.description: Guided across the Arabian Sea from Malindi, da Gama reached Calicut, opening a direct sea route that brought Portuguese traders to Bengal by 1517.
events.significance: Began European maritime empires in Asia.

events.title: Protestant Reformation
events.summary: Martin Luther’s 95 Theses challenged the Catholic Church.
events.description: Spread by the printing press, the Reformation split Western Christianity and led to religious wars and new ideas about conscience and authority.
events.significance: Reshaped European religion and politics.

events.title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
events.summary: Hernán Cortés and indigenous allies captured the Aztec capital.
events.description: Smallpox, alliances with the Tlaxcalans and a long siege brought down the Aztec Empire. The Inca Empire fell to Pizarro soon after.
events.significance: The start of Spanish colonial rule in the Americas.

events.title: Newton’s Principia
events.summary: Isaac Newton set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
events.description: Building on Copernicus, Kepler and Galileo, Newton unified terrestrial and celestial physics with mathematics.
events.significance: The climax of the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Industrial Revolution
events.summary: Mechanised textile production and steam power transformed Britain and then the world.
events.description: Cotton mills, coal and James Watt’s improved steam engine created factory industry. Machine-made British cloth helped destroy Bengal’s handloom textile industry.
events.significance: The beginning of modern economic growth.

events.title: American Declaration of Independence
events.summary: Thirteen British colonies declared independence as the United States.
events.description: Drafted by Thomas Jefferson, the Declaration asserted natural rights. The war ended with the Treaty of Paris (1783).
events.significance: The first successful colonial independence movement.

references.title: Wikipedia – United States Declaration of Independence

events.title: French Revolution
events.summary: The storming of the Bastille began a revolution against absolute monarchy.
events.description: The Declaration of the Rights of Man, the abolition of feudal privileges, the Terror and the rise of Napoleon followed.
events.significance: Spread ideas of liberty, equality and nationalism.

events.title: First Powered Flight
events.summary: The Wright brothers flew the first controlled, powered aeroplane.
events.description: Orville Wright’s first flight lasted 12 seconds. Within decades aviation transformed travel and warfare.
events.significance: The dawn of the air age.

events.title: World War I
events.summary: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand triggered a global war.
events.description: Trench warfare on the Western Front, battles at Gallipoli and the Middle East, and new weapons killed around 20 million people. Over a million Indian soldiers served. The war destroyed four empires: German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman.
events.significance: Redrew the map of Europe and the Middle East.

events.title: Russian Revolution
events.summary: The Tsar was overthrown and the Bolsheviks seized power under Lenin.
events.description: The February Revolution ended the monarchy; the October Revolution brought the Bolsheviks to power. After a civil war the Soviet Union was founded in 1922.
events.significance: Created the world’s first communist state.

events.title: Influenza Pandemic of 1918
events.summary: A flu pandemic infected about a third of humanity.
events.description: Deaths are estimated at 17–50 million or more; British India suffered perhaps 12–17 million deaths, the highest of any region.
events.significance: The deadliest pandemic of the 20th century.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles and the League of Nations
events.summary: The peace treaty imposed harsh terms on Germany and created the League of Nations.
events.description: Reparations and territorial losses fuelled German resentment. Mandates over former Ottoman lands went to Britain and France.
events.significance: Its failures helped lead to World War II.

events.title: The Great Depression
events.summary: The Wall Street Crash triggered a worldwide economic collapse.
events.description: Unemployment soared, trade collapsed and jute and agricultural prices fell, hurting peasants in Bengal. Economic despair helped extremist movements rise in Europe.
events.significance: The worst economic crisis of the industrial era.

events.title: Gandhi’s Salt March
events.summary: Gandhi led a 385 km march to the sea to break the British salt monopoly.
events.description: The non-violent campaign drew global attention and mass participation in civil disobedience.
events.significance: A landmark of non-violent resistance.

events.title: World War II Begins
events.summary: Germany’s invasion of Poland began the deadliest war in history.
events.description: The Axis (Germany, Italy, Japan) fought the Allies (Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States, China and others). Around 70–85 million died, including six million Jews in the Holocaust. Stalingrad (1942–43) turned the tide in the East.
events.significance: Reshaped the global order.

events.title: Pearl Harbor and the Pacific War
events.summary: Japan’s attack brought the United States into the war.
events.description: Japan conquered Southeast Asia and Burma; the Japanese advance on India was stopped at Imphal and Kohima in 1944. Chittagong and Calcutta were bombed.
events.significance: Globalised the war.

events.title: D-Day Landings
events.summary: Allied forces landed in Normandy, opening the Western Front.
events.description: The largest seaborne invasion in history led to the liberation of France and, with the Soviet advance, the defeat of Germany in May 1945.
events.significance: Began the liberation of Western Europe.

events.title: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
events.summary: The United States used nuclear weapons for the first and only time in war.
events.description: Between 110,000 and 210,000 people died. Japan surrendered on 2 September 1945, ending World War II.
events.significance: Began the nuclear age.

references.title: Wikipedia – Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

events.title: United Nations Founded
events.summary: The UN Charter created an organisation to maintain peace and security.
events.description: Founded by 51 states, the UN adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948. Bangladesh joined in 1974.
events.significance: The centre of post-war international cooperation.

events.title: Independence and Partition of India
events.summary: British India was divided into India and Pakistan.
events.description: Partition displaced 10–20 million people and up to two million died in communal violence. It began the wave of decolonisation in Asia and Africa.
events.significance: The largest mass migration of the 20th century.

events.title: People’s Republic of China
events.summary: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People’s Republic after the Communist victory in the civil war.
events.description: The Nationalists retreated to Taiwan. China later went through the Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution and, from 1978, Deng Xiaoping’s reforms.
events.significance: Created a new great power in Asia.

events.title: The Cold War
events.summary: Rivalry between the US-led West and the Soviet bloc divided the world.
events.description: NATO (1949) and the Warsaw Pact (1955), the nuclear arms race, and proxy wars in Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan defined the era. In 1971 the US and China backed Pakistan while the USSR backed India and Bangladesh.
events.significance: Shaped global politics for four decades.

events.title: Korean War
events.summary: North Korea invaded the South; UN forces and China joined the war.
events.description: An armistice in 1953 left Korea divided along the DMZ, without a peace treaty.
events.significance: The first major armed conflict of the Cold War.

events.title: Sputnik and the Space Race
events.summary: The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite.
events.description: Sputnik’s beeping signal shocked the West and began the Space Race. NASA was created in 1958.
events.significance: The beginning of the space age.

events.title: Decolonisation of Africa and Asia
events.summary: Dozens of nations won independence from European empires.
events.description: Ghana (1957) led sub-Saharan Africa; 17 African states became independent in 1960 alone. Algeria won a brutal war against France (1962). The Bandung Conference (1955) and the Non-Aligned Movement gave new states a voice.
events.significance: The end of European colonial empires.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin – First Human in Space
events.summary: Gagarin orbited the Earth in Vostok 1.
events.description: The 108-minute flight made the Soviet cosmonaut a global hero.
events.significance: Humanity’s first journey into space.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.summary: The US and USSR came close to nuclear war over Soviet missiles in Cuba.
events.description: After a naval quarantine and secret negotiations between Kennedy and Khrushchev, the missiles were withdrawn in exchange for US guarantees.
events.significance: The closest the world came to nuclear war.

events.title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
events.summary: "That’s one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind."
events.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed in the Sea of Tranquillity while Michael Collins orbited above.
events.significance: The first humans to walk on another world.

events.title: ARPANET – Birth of the Internet
events.summary: The first message was sent between UCLA and Stanford Research Institute.
events.description: Packet switching and later TCP/IP (1983) allowed networks to interconnect, forming the Internet.
events.significance: The foundation of the digital world.

events.title: Microprocessor and Personal Computers
events.summary: The Intel 4004 put a computer’s CPU on a single chip.
events.description: Microprocessors made personal computers possible: the Apple II (1977), IBM PC (1981) and Macintosh (1984) brought computing into homes and offices.
events.significance: The Technology Revolution.

events.title: End of the Vietnam War
events.summary: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, reunifying Vietnam.
events.description: The long war killed millions of Vietnamese and over 58,000 Americans, and transformed public opinion in the US.
events.significance: A defining conflict of the Cold War.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.summary: East Germans crossed the wall freely as communist regimes fell across Eastern Europe.
events.description: Germany reunified on 3 October 1990.
events.significance: Symbolised the end of the Cold War.

references.title: Wikipedia – Fall of the Berlin Wall

events.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.summary: The USSR broke up into 15 independent states.
events.description: Gorbachev’s reforms, economic crisis and nationalist movements led to its collapse. Five Muslim-majority Central Asian republics became independent.
events.significance: Ended the Cold War and left the US as the sole superpower.

references.title: Wikipedia – Dissolution of the Soviet Union

events.title: World Wide Web Invented
events.summary: Tim Berners-Lee created the Web at CERN.
events.description: Combining hypertext with the Internet, the Web (HTML, HTTP, URLs) became publicly available in 1991 and made the Internet accessible to everyone.
events.significance: Launched the Information Age.

events.title: End of Apartheid
events.summary: Nelson Mandela became South Africa’s first democratically elected president.
events.description: Released in 1990 after 27 years in prison, Mandela led a peaceful transition from apartheid.
events.significance: A triumph of reconciliation over racial oppression.

events.title: September 11 Attacks
events.summary: Terrorist attacks killed nearly 3,000 people in the United States.
events.description: The US-led "war on terror" followed, including wars in Afghanistan (2001–2021) and Iraq (2003–2011).
events.significance: Reshaped global security and politics.

events.title: Human Genome Project Completed
events.summary: Scientists mapped the human genome.
events.description: The international project sequenced about 3 billion DNA base pairs, transforming medicine and biology.
events.significance: Foundation of genomic medicine.

events.title: Internet Era: Social Media and Smartphones
events.summary: Facebook (2004), YouTube (2005) and the iPhone (2007) put the Internet in everyone’s pocket.
events.description: Mobile broadband and social platforms connected billions, transforming news, politics, commerce and social movements.
events.significance: The connected society.

events.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
events.summary: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake caused tsunamis that killed about 230,000 people in 14 countries.
events.description: Aceh in Indonesia was worst hit; Sri Lanka, India and Thailand also suffered. It led to the Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System.
events.significance: One of the deadliest natural disasters in history.

references.title: Wikipedia – 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami

events.title: Global Financial Crisis
events.summary: The collapse of the US housing bubble triggered a global recession.
events.description: Lehman Brothers’ bankruptcy (15 September 2008) froze credit markets; governments bailed out banks.
events.significance: The worst downturn since the Great Depression.

events.title: Arab Spring
events.summary: Protests spread across the Arab world after Mohamed Bouazizi’s self-immolation in Tunisia.
events.description: Rulers fell in Tunisia, Egypt, Libya and Yemen, while Syria descended into a long civil war. Social media played a key role in mobilisation.
events.significance: Reshaped the politics of the Middle East and North Africa.

events.title: Paris Climate Agreement
events.summary: Nearly every country agreed to limit global warming to well below 2 °C.
events.description: Climate-vulnerable countries such as Bangladesh pushed for the 1.5 °C goal and support for adaptation and loss and damage.
events.significance: The central framework for global climate action.

events.title: AlphaGo Defeats Lee Sedol
events.summary: DeepMind’s AI beat a world champion at Go, 4–1.
events.description: Combining deep neural networks and reinforcement learning, AlphaGo achieved what experts expected to take another decade.
events.significance: A milestone in the AI Revolution.

events.title: "Attention Is All You Need" – The Transformer
events.summary: Google researchers introduced the Transformer architecture.
events.description: Self-attention replaced recurrence in sequence models, enabling large language models such as BERT, GPT, Claude and Gemini.
events.significance: The architecture behind modern generative AI.

references.title: Wikipedia – Attention Is All You Need

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.summary: A new coronavirus caused a global pandemic and lockdowns.
events.description: The WHO declared a pandemic in March 2020. Over 7 million deaths were officially reported (excess-death estimates are much higher). mRNA vaccines were developed in under a year.
events.significance: The most disruptive global health crisis in a century.

events.title: Russian Invasion of Ukraine
events.summary: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
events.description: The largest war in Europe since 1945 caused massive casualties, displaced millions and disrupted global food and energy markets.
events.significance: A major shock to the international order.

events.title: Generative AI Goes Mainstream
events.summary: ChatGPT’s release brought large language models to hundreds of millions of people.
events.description: Assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini spread rapidly in education, research and work. Governments responded with rules such as the EU AI Act (2024).
events.significance: The AI Revolution reaches everyday life.

events.title: Chandrayaan-3 Lands Near the Lunar South Pole
events.summary: India became the first country to soft-land near the Moon’s south pole.
events.description: The Vikram lander and Pragyan rover studied the lunar surface, showing the growing role of Asian space programmes.
events.significance: A new era of space exploration beyond the superpowers.
